one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent adopted a two-level (then two/three-level) parametric distribution family that is fundamentally incapable of simultaneously satisfying both KL(P||U)=10 and KL(U||P)=10, and then repeatedly saved and submitted noncompliant results despite clear tolerance violations across eight attempted solver versions.
t_err_evidence: I'll try a two-parameter family of distributions... a fraction of the probability mass uniformly distributed over a subset of the vocabulary
t_commit_evidence: At step 6 the agent receives unambiguous evidence that the two-level approach fails tolerance (forward KL error 0.028, backward KL error 0.003 — actually forward 9.97 vs 10, backward 9.997 vs 10), yet instead of switching to a fundamentally different solver it creates v2, v3, v4, v5, v6, v7, and 'last/quick/fixed' variants all within the same inadequate parametric family, locking in the failing approach.
t_surface_evidence: Forward error: 0.028474 Backward error: 0.003301 FAILED: Could not find distribution within tolerance
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks the domain/algorithmic knowledge that a two-level grouped distribution is provably insufficient for simultaneously achieving KL(P||U)=10 and KL(U||P)=10 with V=150000, and does not know to apply a Newton-based or bisection solve over a three-level (or richer) construction. All subsequent attempts remain within the same restricted model family.
